extracted.intended_audience: journalists, future journalists, and teachers of journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for journalism education and professional development as stated by The Poynter Institute, describing program format, instructional approach, values, and outcomes for participants. Useful for designing or evaluating journalism training and professional practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small seminars / individual attention
rubrics_metrics.description: We keep seminars small, which means you get lots of individual attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes intimate class sizes so participants receive personal support and one-to-one conversation in break-out areas; part of the 'Poynter Experience' that shapes every course and seminar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on, participatory learning
rubrics_metrics.description: We emphasize a hands-on approach, so you participate in discussions, case studies, role-playing, and other exercises to get you involved in learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction is active rather than purely lecture-based; learning methods include role-playing and case studies to simulate real newsroom situations and practice skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished resident and visiting faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Our resident faculty includes distinguished professionals and scholars, all master teachers who bring special expertise to every session. Each seminar also includes visiting faculty, accomplished professionals who leave their jobs for a week to help teach, who spend time with you inside and outside the classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine long-term academic faculty with short-term practicing professionals to provide both theoretical grounding and current industry perspectives; visiting faculty engage beyond formal sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial independence and mission-focus
rubrics_metrics.description: As a financially independent, nonprofit organization, the Institute is beholden to no interest except its own mission: to help journalists do their best work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional independence is presented as a quality criterion ensuring programs prioritize journalistic standards and educator-driven goals rather than commercial or political interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to excellence and editorial integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: It promotes excellence and integrity in the practice of craft and in the practical leadership of successful businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poynter centers both craft-level excellence (reporting, writing, editing) and ethical/editorial integrity; these are core evaluative standards for programs and participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism's civic purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: It stands for a journalism that informs citizens and enlightens public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames quality journalism in terms of its democratic function—informing citizens and improving public discourse—as a standard against which work should be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation to produce great journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: We want you to leave Poynter better prepared to produce great journalism, so that your readers, viewers, or listeners can make better-informed decisions and lead more satisfying lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome-focused: programs should materially improve participants' ability to produce journalism that serves audiences; success measured by participants' readiness and impact on audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipping with new tools and ideas for quality production
rubrics_metrics.description: We want you to be equipped with new tools and ideas to handle the challenges of producing quality news reports, programs, and publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training includes practical tools and conceptual approaches for contemporary news production challenges; emphasizes adaptability and up-to-date methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage to take risks and strive for one's best
rubrics_metrics.description: The courage to take risks and to do your best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values risk-taking in pursuit of stronger journalism; encourages pushing beyond comfort zones as part of professional growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional self-confidence and career agency
rubrics_metrics.description: A higher sense of self-esteem and the power to shape your own career.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs aim to build journalists' confidence and agency, enabling them to direct their career trajectories and make bold professional choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improved craft confidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should leave with concrete improvements in core journalistic skills and the confidence to apply them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of diversity's value
rubrics_metrics.description: A recognition of the value of diversity in the newsroom and in life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes diverse perspectives as a quality criterion for newsroom practice and storytelling; curricula should foster inclusivity and awareness of diverse communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulation of professional purpose (vocabulary)
rubrics_metrics.description: The vocabulary to describe what you do and why, and what you stand for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should help journalists explain and justify their work—useful for leadership, audience engagement, and ethical clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to ongoing growth and sharing knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: A desire to continue your growth as a journalist and to share what you've learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instills a norm of lifelong learning and mentorship; evaluation includes whether participants continue professional development and disseminate lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building a supportive professional network
rubrics_metrics.description: A new network of people who support you in your work, so your learning continues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Networking and peer support are explicit program outcomes; judged by the relationships and continuing exchanges participants gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding journalism's role in democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: A clear picture of the special role of journalism in a democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs emphasize civic-mindedness and the ethical responsibilities of journalists as a criterion of effective training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of the value and impact of one's work
rubrics_metrics.description: An understanding that your life's work is valuable and that you can make a difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivates professional purpose and motivation; success includes participants' belief in journalism's societal impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards drawn from institutional legacy
rubrics_metrics.description: In the development of all its programs, the Institute continues to draw on the standards of excellence set by Nelson Poynter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical and institutional standards (editorial excellence, independence) shape program content and expectations; used as an evaluative benchmark.
